about.bio: Software engineer and team lead with over 5 years of experience.
about.name: Rustambek Abdusalomov
about.story1: In July 2026 I went to Turkey on a trip. Every morning I spent just 5–10 minutes writing a few tickets, and when I came back to the hotel in the evening, they were waiting for me as tested pull requests. Reviewing them took only 10–15 minutes. So 20–25 minutes a day was enough to keep my project work moving, and I can honestly say it made a big difference to how good the trip was. That week I was truly thankful to myself for building agnts.
about.story2: I started it in May, after seeing how much of a developer’s day still goes to reading tickets, explaining them to AI, then checking and testing the result. The first version started working on my own tickets at the end of June, and it has been working on them ever since.
about.story3: When I came back, I told my programmer friends about it, and they got interested. They wanted to try it too, so I opened accounts for them, and soon after, every one of them gave me honest, positive feedback. That’s when agnts became a startup: I concluded that other developers should also spend their time on architecture, scaling and business logic rather than on repetitive daily tasks. I saw for myself how much it raises productivity, and how it lets projects be built with better, more polished solutions.
about.story4: The mobile app is now in testing. I’m building it so the whole process can be managed from a phone. Once testing is done, I plan to launch it in full so everyone can use it.
about.title: I wrote tickets over breakfast. By evening, they were ready for review.

problem.label: Why agnts
problem.title: AI writes the code. You still do everything around it.
problem.lead: Developers already code with AI. But the ticket still has to be read, explained, checked, tested and closed by hand.

p1.title: You turn every ticket into a prompt
p1.text: Read the ticket, dig through the code, then explain the task to the AI in enough detail that it gets it right.

p2.title: You check and test what it wrote
p2.text: Run the build, the linter and the tests, and fix what broke before anyone else sees it.

p3.title: You do the paperwork
p3.text: Push the branch, open the pull request, move the ticket to done.

p4.title: It repeats the same mistakes
p4.text: The AI forgets your corrections, so you explain them again on the next ticket.

s4.title: It learns from every mistake
